a: A stack trace shows the call chain at the moment of an error — read from the top/bottom depending on language.
Common levels: DEBUG, INFO, WARNING, ERROR, CRITICAL.
finally runs whether or not an exception occurred — use for cleanup.
assert checks a condition in development; failure raises an error.
When debugging, isolate: reproduce, reduce inputs, check assumptions, verify each step.
Print/log intermediate values; remove or gate logs before production.
A breakpoint pauses execution in a debugger so you can inspect state.
A heisenbug seems to change behavior when you try to observe/debug it.
Dereferencing null/None causes crashes; check before use or use safe types.
Timeouts mean an operation took too long — raise limits carefully or fix slow dependency.
Connection refused usually means nothing is listening on that host:port.
CORS errors appear in the browser; fix Access-Control headers on the API origin.
Only retry safely if the operation is idempotent or guarded by an idempotency key.
A circuit breaker stops calling a failing dependency temporarily to allow recovery.
Graceful degradation keeps core features working when optional services fail.
